text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi, facing possible trial for alleged abuse of office during his chairmanship of state industrial holding IRI, said the truth had been badly distorted."There has been a false and deceitful reading of the facts" he said. Prodi has received full support from President Oscar Luigi Scalfato, but hard-left Communist Refoundation party along with opposition say Scalfaro should have remained impartial (all).

* In an interview, Foreign minister and leader of Italian Renewal party Lamberto Dini, who recently forced the government to modify the controversial Euro-tax, says his party is ready to leave the ruling coalition if another mistake is committed. "I said to them they cannot go ahead with a 12.5 trillion lire measure (such as the Eurotax) without consulting us...Another mistake like this, and the breaking off between us and the government will be inevitable." (La Stampa).
* In an interview, Defence minister Beniamino Andreatta does not rule out the need for an additional mini-budget next spring to meet the conditions for joining EMU (Corriere della Sera).
* The political dialogue over constitutional reforms is set to start out again between leftist PDS leader Massimo D'Alema and opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi (all).

* In an interview, Giuseppe Falcone, chairman of ailing Banco di Napoli, says he would favour an alliance between insurance company INA, Treasury-controlled Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and Mediocredito centrale to buy the 60 percent stake the Treasury is selling in the southern bank. INA and BNL have already joined forces stating a preliminary interest in the bid (Repubblica).
* Majority parties discussed the proposal raised by the centre-right opposition to abolish a measure, included in the 1997 budget, which say that pensioners cannot have working incomes (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
